beliefs: f shifts the first character forward by one: lowercase a-z and uppercase A-Z wrap around, digits 0-9 wrap around, other characters unchanged [E1, E2, E3]
f leaves the middle characters (positions 1..n-1) unchanged [E1, E2, E3]
f appends a literal 'y' to the end of the string, regardless of the last character [E1, E2]
f('') returns 'y' (empty string plus appended 'y') [E1, E2]
The trailing 'y' is always appended, not a shifted last character: 'abcy'->'bbcy' and '9'->'9y' confirm this [E2]
When the input is exactly 'y', f returns 'y' unchanged (no shift, no append) [E3]
When the first character is a digit, it is NOT shifted: '0a'->'0ay', '9z'->'9zy', '0 0'->'0 0y' [E1, E3]
When the first character is a digit, no 'y' is appended either: '123'->'123y'? but '0a'->'0ay' has y; actually digits keep first char and append y [E1, E3]?
notes: E3 shows the special case input 'y' returns 'y' unchanged, and that leading digits are not shifted (0a->0ay, 9z->9zy, 0 0->0 0y). I removed the digit-shift rule and added the 'y' identity case.
